verdict.rationale: Fern ships its own CLI that can validate API definitions and publish docs and SDKs, and Fern Agent can run on a schedule to produce reports and open pull requests. Together these show scriptable, unattended automation. No evidence explicitly documents running in CI, a non-interactive mode, or token-based auth. The JSON-speaking CLI in the evidence describes CLIs Fern generates for customers' APIs, not Fern's own CLI. Missing for 10: explicit CI/CD integration docs (e.g. GitHub Actions), non-interactive/token auth for headless runs, machine-readable output from the Fern CLI itself, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The Fern CLI lets you initialize projects, validate API definitions, preview changes locally, and publish documentation and SDKs.
You can now put Fern Agent on a schedule
Automations can review your reader feedback, unanswered Ask Fern questions, search queries, or analytics, report back what it found, and open a pull request when the prompt asks for a change.
